To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the likelihood function of a regression model that includes a stochastic trend component depends on the type of trend model, and that the probability of the estimated trend being deterministic is very sensitive on the type of likelihood used.

(i) the probability of estimating a stochastic trend to be deterministic can be quite high, (ii) this probability is very sensitive to whether the likelihood function includes or excludes the stochastic trend in its definition, (iii) the probability can be reduced by including more information in the likelihood function, and (iv) the probability is reduced by using a more efficient estimator of the trend.
the probability of rejecting a true null hypothesis of deterministic trend is very sensitive to whether or not the likelihood function is adjusted for the stochastic trend.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the maximum likelihood estimation of regression models with stochastic trend components.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the model under consideration, the likelihood function should be constructed so that it does not impose any restrictions on the parameters of the trend.

, in the absence of any a priori information on the nature of the trend component, it is preferable to estimate the trend as being stochastic, and that, in the case where a deterministic trend component is suspected, it is better to use a likelihood function which is based on a deterministic trend component.

, for the type of data and model considered here, the likelihood function based on the assumption that the trend is stochastic should be used in preference to the likelihood function based that the trend is deterministic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the likelihood ratio statistic is not an adequate test for the stochastic trend hypothesis, and that a likelihood-based test is preferable.
the likelihood function based on the observed data should not be used for the purpose of estimating a stochastic trend model.
we have found a way of estimating the trend component in a regression model that is robust against the type of likelihood being employed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the likelihood function used to estimate the model has to be chosen carefully, especially in the presence of stochastic trend components.
the probability of incorrectly estimating the stochastic trend as a deterministic trend is much higher than previously reported in the literature.

the likelihood function is an important component of any estimation procedure and that the choice of likelihood function should be based on a careful examination of the underlying data generating process.
